cards.text: Solomon, son of David and king of Israel (2 Chronicles 1:1), has finished the work on the temple of the LORD (2 Chronicles 5:1). He's just prayed a long prayer, kneeling in front of the whole assembly of Israel with his hands spread toward heaven (2 Chronicles 6:13). Now he's done praying, and the burnt offering and the sacrifices are waiting.

cards.question: Solomon finishes praying. What comes down from heaven and consumes the burnt offering and the sacrifices?
The offerings are consumed. Then the glory of the LORD ___ the temple.
With the glory of the LORD filling the house, the priests walk right in to serve.

cards.text: Out in the courtyard, all the Israelites are watching. They see the fire coming down and the glory of the LORD above the temple.

cards.question: The Israelites see the fire and the glory of the LORD above the temple. What do they do on the pavement?

answers.text: Bow with faces to the ground
Run back toward the city gates
Stand still and cover their eyes

cards.text: Then they worship and give thanks to the LORD: “For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.” A huge crowd, faces on the pavement, and nobody, NOBODY, is checking the time.
Then the king and all the people offer sacrifices before the LORD, and King Solomon offers 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. Friend, I start sweating when a batch hits TWO DOZEN.

cards.question: With all these sacrifices, the king and all the people ___ the house of God.

cards.text: The priests stand at their posts. The Levites pick up the musical instruments of the LORD, the same ones someone once used to praise Him, saying, “For His loving devotion endures forever.”

cards.question: Who made the Levites' instruments for giving thanks to the LORD?
While the priests sound trumpets across from the Levites, all the Israelites are standing.

cards.text: Then Solomon consecrates the middle of the courtyard, right in front of the house of the LORD. That's where he offers the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings.

cards.question: Why does Solomon offer them in the middle of the courtyard instead of on the bronze altar he made?

answers.text: The bronze altar can't hold them all
The bronze altar isn't finished yet
The crowd wants a closer look

cards.text: Solomon and all Israel are together, a very great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt. If this were a group chat, my phone would NEVER stop buzzing.

cards.question: Solomon and this huge assembly keep the feast for ___ days.
The feast wraps up. On the eighth day, what do they hold?

cards.text: Why an eighth day? Because the dedication of the altar had lasted seven days, and the feast seven days more. Two whole weeks, friend, and I need a nap after ONE long day at the oven.

cards.question: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sends the people home. How do they go?

cards.text: They're glad for the good things the LORD did for David, for Solomon and for His people Israel. Hold onto that feeling, friend, because this story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The question says "Why does Solomon offer them" without naming what "them" is. The burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings are only named on card 13, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Joyful and glad of heart," uses the BSB's wording and sounds more like the Bible than the plain modern wrong answers ("Tired and ready to rest," "Quiet and a little worried"). That makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. The 11 choice cards are 6 multiple choice (cards 2, 6, 11, 14, 17, 19), 3 fill in the blank and only 2 true or false.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
